name: Question 13
problem:
Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(t)$ given that its derivative ${r}^{′}(t)$ and the derivative of the corresponding unit tangent ${T}^{′}(t)$ are as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t)=\,i-\frac{t}{\sqrt{4-{t}^{2}}}\,j,\,{T}^{′}(t)=-\frac{t}{2\sqrt{4-{t}^{2}}}\,i-\frac{1}{2}\,j\end{aligned}
$$
worked_solution:
Since we are given both the derivative of the curve ${r}^{′}(t)$ and the derivative of the unit tangent ${T}^{′}(t)$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

Now, we find the magnitudes of ${r}^{′}(t)$ and ${T}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{(-\frac{t}{\sqrt{4-{t}^{2}}})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+\frac{{t}^{2}}{4-{t}^{2}}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{4-{t}^{2}+{t}^{2}}{4-{t}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{4-{t}^{2}}} \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(-\frac{t}{2\sqrt{4-{t}^{2}}})}^{2}+{(-\frac{1}{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{{t}^{2}}{4(4-{t}^{2})}+\frac{1}{4}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{{t}^{2}+4-{t}^{2}}{4(4-{t}^{2})}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{4-{t}^{2}}}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{(\frac{1}{\sqrt{4-{t}^{2}}})}{(\frac{2}{\sqrt{4-{t}^{2}}})}=\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 13

Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve r(t) given that its derivative r′(t) and the derivative of the corresponding unit tangent T′(t) are as follows:

r′(t)=i−t4−t2j,T′(t)=−t24−t2i−12j

a
2
b
4
c
1
d
12
e
14
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since we are given both the derivative of the curve r′(t) and the derivative of the unit tangent T′(t), we will use the following formula for the curvature: κ(t)=‖T′(t)‖‖r′(t)‖

Now, we find the magnitudes of r′(t) and T′(t): ‖r′(t)‖=12+(−t4−t2)2=1+t24−t2=4−t2+t24−t2=24−t2‖T′(t)‖=(−t24−t2)2+(−12)2=t24(4−t2)+14=t2+4−t24(4−t2)=14−t2 Hence, the curvature is κ(t)=‖T′(t)‖‖r′(t)‖=(14−t2)(24−t2)=12.
